prompt: You know a production nginx config has a setting called `worker_connections` that was recently changed, but you don't know which commit or even which branch touched it. Which command finds every commit that added or removed that exact string?
choices: git log -S"worker_connections" --oneline --all
git diff HEAD~10 HEAD
git blame worker_connections
git status --short

prompt: Why should `*.tfstate` files be listed in `.gitignore` for a Terraform infrastructure repo rather than committed?
choices: Terraform state files are often very large and slow down clones
Git cannot diff binary files like .tfstate
State files can contain plaintext secrets pulled from provider APIs and should live in a remote backend, not version control
Terraform refuses to run if state files are tracked by git

prompt: After resolving a merge conflict in a Terraform .tf file by combining both sides' changes and removing the conflict markers, what should you do before committing the resolution?
choices: Immediately run terraform apply to confirm the merge worked
Run terraform plan to validate the resulting resource graph before committing
Nothing extra is needed since git already confirmed the merge is correct
Force-push the merge commit to skip CI

prompt: You're mid-edit on an Ansible playbook with changes that don't compile cleanly yet, when an incident requires you to switch to a clean main branch immediately. What is the correct move?
choices: git commit the broken changes so you don't lose them, then switch branches
git stash push -m "..." to shelve the changes, then switch branches
git reset --hard to discard the changes and start the hotfix fresh
Open a second terminal and manually copy the file contents aside

prompt: After fixing an incident on a hotfix branch, you return to your stashed work with `git stash pop` and the stashed file overlaps with a file the hotfix also touched. What happens?
choices: git silently discards the stash to avoid any risk
git automatically keeps the hotfix version and drops the stash changes
You get a conflict with standard <<<<<<< markers, resolved the same way as a merge conflict
git refuses to pop and permanently deletes the stash

prompt: You want to see which commits exist on origin/main that you don't yet have locally, before merging them into a branch you're about to apply to production. Which sequence does that safely?
choices: git pull origin main, then inspect the result afterward
git fetch origin, then git log main..origin/main --oneline
git merge origin/main directly without looking first
git clone the repo again into a new directory

prompt: A bad config commit has been identified as the cause of a production outage. Why is git revert generally preferred over git reset for undoing it on a shared branch?
choices: git revert is faster to execute than git reset
git revert creates a new commit that undoes the change while preserving history, instead of rewriting history others may have already pulled
git reset only works on remote branches, not local ones
git revert automatically runs terraform apply after undoing the change

prompt: Given a commit hash a3f9c21, which command shows exactly what that single commit changed, including the diff?
choices: git log --oneline -- a3f9c21
git stash show a3f9c21
git show a3f9c21
git branch a3f9c21
